_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local clusters for band1_lower_meadows. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. Existing entries keep the index they had before the split because the merged array order is the order props are added to the scene tree, and Godot silently auto-renames same-named siblings by that order. A new entry in this band takes an unused order in this band's reserved range 1000-1999, which no other band can collide with; do not renumber an existing one.

props._why: the cluster's anchor -- an anvil mounted on its own stump
faces the anvil across the nook -- pulled in 0.7m (round 1 blind critic: the anvil/whetstone and crate/workbench read as two separate groups, not one station)
a sharpening stone within reach of the bench -- pulled in 0.4m, same reason
stock crate behind the anvil -- pulled in 0.9m, same reason
a tool left leaning, mid-repair -- pulled in 0.3m, same reason
the cluster's anchor -- overflow from the last harvest

set right against the barrel's side, not just nearby -- round 2 blind critic: a loose arc of props near a wall reads as dumped, not a task. This is meant to read as one pile: a load just carried out and set down together.

touching the barrel's other side, tipped at an angle rather than square -- just set down, not arranged. FarmCrate_Carrot swapped out earlier (round 1 blind critic): its vertex-colour-tinted contents render as an unreadable white/grey smear, a model defect not a placement one.
in front of the pile, facing back toward it -- the tool that did the carrying, set down after
the big piece of the same load, closing the pile from the front

EV7-clusters-fix: the cluster's anchor -- a travelling trainer's pack, dropped beside the practice-meadow path, kept as its own separate stop rather than crammed against the supply pile (a genuine blind critic on the shipped state: 'reads as three container props at even spacing... scatter-list output, not a place'). Sited off route 2 ([18,-24]->[30,-40], terrain_playground.json), inside the practice-meadow clearing (vegetation.json, centre [30,-40] r16) but well short of the arena itself.

EV7-clusters-fix: the pile's anchor. This meadow slopes here for real -- a corner-height probe against the crate's own exact footprint (tools/_probe_ev7fix.gd) measures 0.137-0.172m of spread across the headings tried, barely moved by yaw alone (165deg: 0.137m vs the old -25deg heading's 0.145m -- yaw was never going to fix this on its own). `sink_m` 0.08 is what actually settles it: added to the model's own ~0.05m embed, the crate's rigid bottom sits ~0.13m below the sampled centre height, which is deeper than half this footprint's worst-case corner spread, so every corner ends up buried in the terrain mesh rather than floating above it, regardless of which way it's turned. `Bench` (a trestle table) is DROPPED entirely -- the critic's own offered alternative ('drop the table and commit to a supply cache at a waypoint composition'): props.gd places every prop flush to the ground with no way to rest one ON another, so the table's flat top could never actually hold the crate/sack/barrel it was meant to -- they always passed clean through its legs. A cache of things set down together, not a furnished stop, is what this system can honestly build.

EV7-clusters-fix: touching the crate's side (0.83m centre-to-centre, matching the two footprints' combined radius) so the pair reads as one pile someone set down together, not a scatter -- distinct spacing from the pack 1.9m away, breaking the old even 3-way spacing the critic named as 'placed by script.' Still the plain supply barrel, not the farmhouse's apple-branded one.

EV7-clusters-fix: the cluster's anchor, moved to hug the footbridge's own west landing (tools/_probe_ev7fix.gd -- bridge local frame x=-5.3, z=1.4, just outside the deck/rail collider's z=+/-1.05 half-extent and past the stone abutment tile at local x=-3.9..-5.9) instead of sitting marooned in open lawn ~3m further out (a genuine blind critic on the shipped state: 'marooned ~6m from the house and ~4m off the bridge head in open lawn'). `sink_m` buries the crate's own shallow 0.05m embed a little further so grass doesn't show lit up under its skirt -- this spot is flat (0.000-0.006m corner spread, real terrain data, not sloped), so the old 'floating crate' complaint here was the shallow embed, not a slope.

EV7-clusters-fix: actually leaning against the crate's near face now, not standing bolt upright ('the axe LEVITATES: bolt upright, unsupported, haft ending mid-air'). This model is authored vertical in its own glTF (a baked -90deg node rotation puts its long axis on Y regardless of yaw -- confirmed with tools/_probe_ev7fix.gd, not guessed), so no yaw value could ever lay it down; `pitch_deg` is new on scripts/world/props.gd for exactly this. Anchor and pitch picked from the same probe's world-space AABB check so the tilted mesh's low end sits in the grass and its body actually overlaps the crate's east face (~0.05m real contact, not just visually adjacent), clear of the crate's own footprint so it doesn't clip through a corner.

EV7-clusters-fix: moved to the crate's own east/bridge-facing side, in front rather than tucked behind it ('the rope coil -- the most purpose-carrying prop -- is 90% hidden behind the crate'). This is the side a player sees first walking off the bridge, so the repair stock reads immediately instead of needing to walk around the crate to find it.

EV7-clusters-fix: water bucket at the pile's far (west) side, foot of the pile -- kept off the deck/rail collider the same way the rest of the cluster is now (local z 1.75, not 0.89 like the position this replaced, which was inside the walkway's own collider footprint).

clusters.name: trail_camp

props._why: BAND1-D1-v3, the camp's focus and the fix for round 2's central failure. Two changes, both measured. (1) The asset: `Bonfire_Fire.obj`, not `Bonfire.obj`. Round 2 rejected it on the note that its extra surface 'shares the same combined mesh with the logs rather than isolating a flame' -- true of the OBJ file (one object, Bonfire_Fire_Cylinder.009), false of what Godot imports, because the OBJ loader splits by material. tools/_probe_bonfire_fire.gd: 3 surfaces, `Wood`, `LightWood`, `Fire`, and `Fire` is a real flame cone standing 1.63m above the log pile. campfire_glow.gd::ignite() gives that surface an emissive override. (2) The scale: raw AABB 2.18 x 2.31 x 1.98m, so round 2's scale 1.0 put a 2.2m-wide, 1.5m-tall log pile in a camp whose stool is 0.58m tall -- the blind critic read it as 'oversized inert logs' and it was. 0.45 gives a 0.98m fire with a 0.47m log pile under a flame reaching 1.04m. The glow overlay is counter-scaled back out to absolute metres by props.gd, so shrinking the fire does not shrink its own smoke column; that shrinkage is exactly what made the camp invisible from the trail.

Fire-ring stone 1 of six. Replaces round 3's first cut, which built the ring out of stylized_nature's RockPath_Round_* models. Those are the third strike on that family: the round-2 critic called them 'two amorphous blobs ... too bright, no arrangement, reads as litter or snow patches', and shrinking them did not help, because they are not stones -- each one is a flat MOSAIC of pale pebbles (measured 1.06-2.13m across, 0.11m thick, one 'PathRocks' texture), so at any scale it reads as a patch of gravel lying in grass. Rock_Medium_* are actual boulders from the same pack; at 0.11-0.15 of a ~3.2m raw model they are 0.35-0.50m stones, which is what someone rings a fire with.
Fire-ring stone 2 of six -- three models across six stones at six scales, so no two are the same rock at the same size.
Fire-ring stone 3 of six -- three models across six stones at six scales, so no two are the same rock at the same size.
Fire-ring stone 4 of six -- three models across six stones at six scales, so no two are the same rock at the same size.
Fire-ring stone 5 of six -- three models across six stones at six scales, so no two are the same rock at the same size.
Fire-ring stone 6 of six -- three models across six stones at six scales, so no two are the same rock at the same size.

Long seat, 2.78m on its own local x axis (measured, tools/_probe_camp_models.gd), sat tangentially at 2.51m from the fire. The yaw is computed to put that long axis perpendicular to the radius, which is what 'facing the fire' means for a bench -- a 2.8m seat pointing radially out of a fire ring reads wrong whichever way its front happens to face. The model is 0.53m tall with 0.53m depth and no backrest, so the 180-degree ambiguity in that solution does not show.

A third, informal seat -- a felled log rolled up to the fire rather than furniture, breaking the bench/stool's regularity. 1.00m on local x; same tangential yaw rule as the bench. Round 2 had it 2.2m from the bench and both near the same bearing, which is where the critic's 'a long log skewers straight through the wattle panel' came from: the bench IS the wattle-looking panel and log_large was inside it. They are now 2.9m apart on opposite arcs of the ring.

A second, smaller seat on the far side of the fire from the bench. Round 2's critic said it faced the barrel; the barrel has been moved out of its sightline and the yaw is now computed to aim the model's -Z at the fire rather than picked by eye. At 0.51 x 0.58 x 0.53m it is nearly rotationally symmetric, so this mostly matters for not looking deliberate about the wrong thing.

Firewood, not a seat: a 0.71m log lying radially with its end toward the fire, as if part-fed in, and pitched 4 degrees off level so not every prop in the camp stands perfectly axis-upright. Radial here is deliberate and is the opposite rule from the two seats above, for the opposite reason.

Supply crate, moved out to 4.2m behind the bench with the bag and rope. Round 2 stacked crate, bag, rope, backpack and barrel all inside 2.5m of the fire, which is how a camp turns into the 'well-lit prop dump' the critic warned about. Gear lives behind where people sit, not between them and the fire.
Leaning against the crate -- the same 'pile someone set down together' composition the existing trainer_camp/bridge_repair_site clusters use.
Coiled beside the crate/bag pile, the same role it plays at the bridge_repair_site cluster.

The single worst prop in round 2 and the one the critic called a haystack 'parked touching the fire pile'. Measured raw: 3.34 x 3.12 x 1.75m with its origin 1.46m ABOVE its own base. At round 2's scale 0.55 that is a 1.7m-tall pack -- taller than the bench is long is not far off -- sunk 0.80m into the ground, which is exactly the lumpy tan half-buried mass a haystack is. Scale 0.18 gives a 0.60 x 0.56m pack; `sink_m` -0.25 lifts it by the scaled origin offset so it rests on the ground instead of in it. Negative sink is the existing key used the other way round, not a new one.

Water barrel (measured 0.70 x 0.90 x 0.70m, already the right size at scale 1.0 -- round 2 was right about that and it is left alone). Moved to the camp's west edge, off the line between the stool and the fire it used to sit on.

First of six pieces of authored scenery breaking up the camp's outer edge and the wide frame's foreground. The clearing this cluster sits in (vegetation.json order 1000) strips scattered grass for 9m, so without an authored edge the clearing itself becomes the composition problem the round-2 critic named as a '60% empty grass slope'. Raw 1.91m, so 0.42 is a 0.80m bush. environment/nature's plant_bush / grass_large / rock_small* are NOT usable through props.gd, and that finding is why this swap happened: tools/_probe_camp_materials.gd shows every one of them ships a material with NO albedo texture and a flat placeholder colour -- their 'grass' material is albedo (0.45, 0.93, 0.87), which renders as the flat CYAN shards the first round-3 capture scattered all round this camp, and their 'dirt' material is (0.95, 0.74, 0.62), near-white. That pack is authored against a palette atlas the import does not apply. Only its log/log_large survive, and only by luck -- their wood-tan placeholder happens to look like wood. stylized_nature's models all carry real albedo textures, so the camp's scenery comes from there instead.
Flowering variant at the camp's west edge beyond the gear pile -- the same silhouette carrying different colour, rather than a second identical bush.
Fern south of the stool. Raw 2.83m across and only 0.84m tall, so 0.26 gives a 0.74m low spreading clump -- a different SHAPE from the bushes, not a third round mass.
Tall grass tuft on the trail side, in the near foreground of the approach view. 1.15 x 1.61m raw -> 0.58 x 0.81m.
Low clover clump south-west, at ground level where the bushes are not, so the camp's edge is not all one height. Moved 1.4m west of its first position to clear the tent's footprint.
A single larger boulder on the trail side, 0.67m -- bigger than the fire-ring stones so the two read as different things, and something for the eye to land on between the trail and the fire.

The shelter, and the prop that unblocks this camp's acceptance line. Two independent blind critics landed on the same gap -- nothing here said anyone SLEPT here -- and BAND1-D1 round 3 first parked it in ralph/BLOCKED.md as needing owner-supplied reference art. That was wrong, and the owner said so: CLAUDE.md forbids GENERATING without reference art, while 'Asset work' explicitly permits SOURCING a candidate asset. Kenney's Survival Kit (CC0 1.0, docs/ASSET_LEDGER.md) ships a tent, three bedrolls and a fire pit. Chosen over Quaternius's own Survival pack, which is the five models already vendored here (Axe, Backpack, Bonfire, Bonfire_Fire, Knife) and has no shelter. Verified in-engine before placement (tools/_probe_kenney_survival.gd): every surface carries a real `colormap` albedo texture, which is exactly the check environment/nature failed earlier this round. Authored small -- raw 0.56 x 0.49 x 0.56m -- so scale 3.5 gives a 1.96m one-person tent, sized against the 0.90m barrel and the 2.78m bench beside it rather than by eye. Sited BEYOND the fire on the camp's south arc, not on its north-west one: the first cut put it north-west, where it stood on ground 0.30m above the fire (measured) and, from all three authored viewpoints, sat between the camera and the camp instead of behind it. From here it is a silhouette behind the flame in the close view and behind the smoke column on the road approach, and it never occludes the glow that is what actually carries at range. Yaw was tested both ways against the render rather than trusted from the maths: at +90 the tent presents a closed canvas wall to the camp and the bedroll disappears behind it; at the computed face-the-fire value the open gable and the bedroll inside it both read. A shelter you cannot see into is a shed.

The bedroll, laid at the tent's mouth with its long axis pointing out toward the fire. The tent carries the silhouette at distance; this is the detail that does the same work up close, where a canvas shape alone still reads as equipment rather than as somebody's night. Raw 0.31 x 0.12 x 0.61m with its long axis on local z, so scale 3.0 gives 0.93 x 0.36 x 1.83m -- a real bedroll's footprint. `bedroll-frame` and `bedroll-packed` were vendored alongside it and are unused for now: a packed roll is what a traveller carries, not what an occupied camp leaves out.

clusters._why: BAND1-D1-v3. Relocated from (348,919) to (344,935). The old site drops 1.2m across the camp's own 7m footprint (tools/_probe_camp_ground.gd), which is why round 2's props sat at nine different heights and why the wide frame read as a grass slope with objects on it. tools/_probe_camp_flat.gd swept the ground 5-14m off the loop trail and (344,935) is the flattest shelf near it: 0.29m of relief across 8m, 7.8m from the trail's (300,880)-(370,950) leg. A camp is a place someone chose to stop; the ground has to look like a reason to choose it.
